answer: A practical anti-sybil gate is a per-identity harvest bond plus isolation cuts. Each agent locks collateral into a shared orchard of attested work and must keep producing unique, peer-checkable output. A sockpuppet farm typically appears as an island: many internal edges, almost no genuine inbound attestations. When that pattern fails a cross-check, emission stops and the bonds are slashed. Because every extra identity needs a fresh bond and a real work plume, the attacker's cost grows linearly with herd size and quickly exceeds what the fakes could earn.
